checks.what: The prepared input-manifest delta from c020 is exactly tools/audit_public.py and tests/test_audit_public.py; C, assembly, names, classification and data inputs are unchanged. Subsequent worktree fixes were detected during review, so final adversarial checks and tests use immutable 8244974 copies whose SHA-256 hashes equal the c021 prepare record: audit bfd7461168cdc748e7a1587586246ea13d9af40b12a1a68e966fe5af9697f13b; tests 4523abdfe60776cfc775ae286957a3f3fdb740ff7252841245f727b1d8a22e34. This verdict does not assess the in-progress c022 fixes.

Challenged expression masking with Base85, Z85, Base64, URL-safe Base64 and hex through four unary/address/member wrappers each. All twenty generic controls remain caught with ROM references. However, a lossless standard Base85 encoding of 36 consecutive REV 02 bytes at 0x0008d4 wrapped in f(&<encoding>); is accepted by both ROM-aware and ROM-free content checks. The frozen c020 baseline rejects the same source as an opaque Base85 run. The extended flat grammar masks short mixed-case encoded atoms and malformed punctuation sequences; atom opacity checks do not protect atoms below 48 characters.

The copyright-or-binary-vector condition correctly distinguishes the prior text-header false positive from actual headers and still recognizes binary-vector headers without copyright and text-vector headers with copyright. But increasing the minimum from 272 to 276 creates a decoded-payload regression: exact retail prefixes of 272, 273, 274 and 275 bytes, Base64/Base85/hex encoded, now pass ROM-free content checks in both revisions. All 24 cases are rejected by the frozen c020 baseline. The ROM-aware index still catches them. Across 42 immutable header/encoding comparisons there were no ROM-aware misses; separate mutation probes also preserved the known-ROM backstop.

REVIEWED_FALSE_POSITIVES has exactly one complete (40-hex blob id, exact path) key. Independently hashed the actual historical source as a Git blob and obtained 76fd193d0b318c6266751e9eee359c569c3df8a4. In an isolated scratch Git repository, only its matching historical opaque URL-safe Base64 reason is suppressed. Identical content at another path and a changed blob at the original path are reported. Injected independent content/path reasons survive the real filtering control flow. Path reasons and worktree checks are not covered by this exception. No broader suppression was found.

Reproduced the requested exact CLI invocation, tools/audit_public.py --history, with both ROMs: exit 0, PASS, 1085 unique Git blobs, 105 trees, 351 tracked worktree files, 2 ROMs indexed, 0 findings. This clean-repository result does not exercise or disprove the newly demonstrated laundering and truncated-prefix bypasses.

Executed all 60 tests from the immutable c021 audit test module. Fifty-nine passed initially; one encountered a reviewer harness-relative-path error when locating tools/audit_public.py. Corrected only the isolated scratch fixture layout and retried that single test successfully; no product assertion failed and no test was skipped. The new security counterexamples are absent from those passing fixtures.

findings.what: The expanded REFERENCE_EXPRESSION can launder genuine ROM material through the normal ROM-aware public gate. Standard Base85 encoding of REV 02 [0x0008d4,0x0008f8), wrapped as f(&<encoding>);, yields no content_reasons with both reference ROMs indexed, and also none in ROM-free mode. Standard decoding of the inner encoding reproduces the 36 original bytes exactly (SHA-256 4c3f95c47af77f2015053ce573e0d6a4bc6f6b16302887070c7647c69f416238). The pre-delta tool rejects the source as an opaque 50-character Base85 run at entropy 4.659. The flat expression mask accepts encoded punctuation/identifier sequences without establishing legitimate references; its short atoms evade the 48-character opacity threshold. Once masked, the ordinary decoder examines the wrapper-shifted Base85 token and misses the original byte grouping. Exact private reproduction is retained in delta-frozen-checks.json rather than copied into public-source recommendations.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the older expression rule separate from the new unary/member forms and permit only a narrowly validated reference shape with independently justified atoms; do not exempt arbitrary short mixed-case atoms merely because they fit identifier syntax. Add this exact private-ROM counterexample plus synthetic structural equivalents and assert rejection both with ROMs and ROM-free, while retaining the legitimate current-expression positives. The no-Base64-punctuation argument does not establish safety for Base85/Z85 punctuation.

findings.what: The new len(raw) >= 276 condition drops previously detected 272–275-byte Genesis prefixes. Exact first-272/273/274/275-byte prefixes of either retail ROM now pass ROM-free content_reasons when encoded as Base64, Base85 or hex; all 24 corresponding cases are rejected by the frozen prior tool. The inputs retain real binary vectors and SEGA at 0x100, so the false-positive fix does not require excluding them. The normal ROM-aware gate still detects these windows, but the ROM-free embedded-payload defense has regressed, including decoded payloads.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain the previous 272-byte minimum and apply the copyright-or-binary-vector condition without increasing that bound. Slicing the optional copyright field is safe for short buffers, and binary-vector evidence is already available. Add 272–275-byte encoded-prefix regressions in both ROM-aware and ROM-free modes alongside the text-header positive.
